AI Representation: A desert shelter with foraged food, a backpack and discarded goods representing Suelo’s moneyless way of life. Image credits: Chatgpt

The Man Who Quit Money

University of Colorado degree and Peace Corps service in Ecuador

Twelve years of

foraging

and scavenging, 2000 to 2012

Vohs, Mead and Goode's nine money experiments, 2006

USDA food waste estimates for 2010: 133 billion pounds, 31 percent

Moab overlook from Arches. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Suelo's return to financial society, 2015 to 2021

Daniel Shellabarger, who later became known as Daniel Suelo, decided to live without money in autumn 2000 after leaving his last thirty dollars in a phone booth at a truck stop in Pennsylvania, according to an account by Clay Bonnyman Evans published in The Coloradan. Mark Sundeen’s book, published in 2012, gave an account of Suelo’s way of life in the vicinity of Moab, Utah, where Suelo lived in a cave and gathered wild foods, as well as collected leftover food. In a blog post reproduced by Peace Corps Online , Suelo described money as a stand-in for the past as debt and the future as credit, never the present. The man had led a moneyless life, which is different from total self-reliance, since Suelo would accept any freely donated gifts and rejected any money or bartering system. This article looks at Suelo's lifestyle alongside two other sources: a 2006 psychology study on money and a federal report on food waste.Suelo's background appeared ordinary. Peace Corps Online, in a document reprinted in 2009, listed Suelo as a former Peace Corps volunteer in Ecuador who had earned an anthropology degree at the University of Colorado and worked as a lab technician.Furthermore, it is mentioned that he was 48 years old and lived in a cave around one hour away from Moab. The Coloradan’s account, as preserved by Clay Bonnyman Evans, placed him in the class of 1984. The Deseret News reported that he had been depressed for about 10 years before his 2000 decision.Sundeen’s version, as quoted in the blog Citydesert, depicts the 12 years of living without money in which Suelo lived on wild edibles, scavenged food, some roadkill and gifts. An Associated Press profile of Suelo, published in the Summit Daily in 2009, provides additional details. Suelo went through Moab's garbage once a week and found more than enough for himself. Suelo assured the reporter that he never got sick because of the scavenged food.He rejected barter because he saw it as a form of money, the Deseret News reported. In an interview on Becoming Minimalist, he disagreed with the intro calling him boastful for avoiding food stamps and any other government assistance since it might imply that he considers himself superior to those who need such help. Gordon Stevenson, who directed a film about Suelo, talked to AP about the contradiction between Suelo's way of life and his reliance on people who use money. The Coloradan reported in 2013 that he had lived in a cave outside Moab for 13 years. Peace Corps Online's account of his 2000 hitchhike shows he did not stay in one place. In a 2021 profile, Utah Stories reported that he had made a home near Moab during the 1990s, before he gave up money.In The Psychological Consequences of Money , published in Science, Kathleen Vohs, Nicole Mead and Miranda Goode reported nine experiments. The 2006 experiments suggested that money primes a more self-reliant orientation, making people less dependent on others, which offers background on how life without money differs from ordinary financial life. Moreover, they preferred to engage in solitary play, solitary work, and sit themselves at a greater distance from an unfamiliar individual compared to people exposed to neutral terms.The food recovered by Suelo fits into the national pattern, which is well-established. USDA's Economic Research Service published a paper titled "The Estimated Amount, Value, and Calories of Postharvest Food Losses at the Retail and Consumer Levels in the United States." According to the statistics provided there, 133 billion pounds, out of 430 billion pounds of food available for consumption, were wasted in 2010, which is 31% of the available food, retail value of which was estimated at $161.6 billion. According to the estimates provided by the agency, retailers wasted 43 billion pounds of food, which is 10% of the available amount, and consumers wasted 90 billion pounds, which is 21%. The amount of wasted calories amounted to 387 billion per day, and meat, poultry and fish accounted for 30% of the total value lost.The agency reported that there was an average loss of 1,249 calories per person per day. Meat, poultry, and fish constituted 30 percent of the food wasted in terms of value, amounting to $48 billion. Reasons for wastage at the retail level included broken equipment like malfunctioning cold storage, ordering more than required and discarding damaged produce. This is shown by Suelo’s experience of the visible effect of food wastage; however, there are many other kinds of wastage included in the above statistics that cannot be recovered from trash.Utah Stories reported in 2021 that Suelo's moneyless period lasted about 15 years, from 2000 until he returned to financial society in 2015 to care for his parents. A 2021 profile by Utah Stories described him as living in Colorado with his mother. The profile also said that he was still adjusting to life in a money-based society after years without money.
Article Summary: Daniel Shellabarger, who later became known as Daniel Suelo, decided to live without money in autumn 2000. Suelo lived on wild edibles, scavenged food, some roadkill and gifts. In a 2006 psychology study on money, Kathleen Vohs, Nicole Mead and Miranda Goode reported nine experiments. The experiments suggested that money primes a more self-reliant orientation, making people less dependent on others.

Article Title: In 2015, a Washington couple who paid $6.7m for a lakefront home added a children's treehouse and a tram to the beach then listed it for $21.25m
Article Text:
Representative image of a Treehouse. (Image Credits: Pexels)

Representative image of a waterfront home with a dock. (Image Credits: Pexels)

What the mansion offers across three floors

Luxury on the lakeside

A sprawling lakefront estate in Bellevue, Washington, that belongs to former NFL quarterback Russell Wilson and Grammy-winning singer Ciara, is officially in contract to change hands for $21.25 million, according to The Wall Street Journal, which cited a person familiar with the deal. When taken together with the separate sale of an adjacent parcel that held the couple's sports court, completed in 2022 for $9.75 million. The combined real estate transaction for the entire contiguous compound was set to reach $31 million.The transaction follows a two-year marketing effort done for the luxury compound. In April 2022, the 11,100-square-foot Mediterranean-style primary residence announced its arrival in the open real estate market for a premium asking price of $36 million which included the adjacent lot. This closely coincided with the high-profile offseason trade which saw the transfer of Wilson from the Seattle Seahawks to the Denver Broncos.After two separate market price adjustments, the initial asking price of the house, which stood at $28 million on its own, was brought down to $24.9 million, until it was secured by a buyer at a $21.25 million contract. Public property records suggest that Wilson, who married Ciara in July 2016 and shares three children with her, bought the main estate parcel for $6.7 million in 2015 and made a $14.6 million gain on the primary structure alone.Overlooking Lake Washington and the Seattle skyline, the three-story residential estate sits on 1.06 acres of land. Inside, the floor plan accommodates six bedrooms and five full en-suite bathrooms. Additionally, there's a powder room, and all interior levels are made accessible through an integrated three-story elevator system.The main entrance opens into a grand foyer featuring a winding spiral staircase and there’s a chandelier overhead and coffered ceiling. The main-level common area has a fireside living room which is highlighted by a curved wall of glass and an attached formal dining space. While the primary gourmet kitchen includes two Sub-Zero refrigerators and a gas range, all centred around a 14-foot prep island.A primary bedroom suite offers a private terrace access with a wood-burning fireplace and a dedicated alcove seating area. Its attached master bathroom suite boasts dual vanities alongside a soaking tub, a walk-in closet, and an adjoined vanity glamour room with its own fireplace. Elsewhere the home serves as a recreational haven fully equipped with a home theater, an au pair suite, a recording studio, two home offices, a sunroom, two separate fitness studios, and three specialized children’s playrooms.According to Carmen Gayton of Windermere Real Estate Co., who held the listing, the property has 164 feet of prime waterfront along Lake Washington with a boat dock, plus a tram down to the water or 77 steps for anyone who wants the exercise. While on the outside, the manicured grounds are replete with premier outdoor living, fire pits and an integrated hot tub. What stands out is a two-story treehouse which serves as a whimsical centerpiece with a spiral staircase and storybook-inspired green cladding. The couple added both the treehouse and the tram. Since, the estate sits along Lake Washington, shoreline improvements can also be subject to local permitting requirements. Bellevue requires a Shoreline Management Conditional Use permit for certain regulated shoreline uses.The closing of the Washington assets follows with other sales in their real estate portfolio. Following his release from the Denver Broncos in March 2024 and his subsequent signing of a $1.2 million contract for one year with the Pittsburgh Steelers, the family offloaded their Cherry Hills Village mansion near Denver.
Article Summary: The three-story residential estate sits on 1.06 acres of land. Inside, the floor plan accommodates six bedrooms and five en-suite bathrooms. The main-level common area has a fireside living room which is highlighted by a curved wall of glass and an attached formal dining space.

Article Title: In 1988, a Malibu developer and his wife bought land for $1.7 million, built a 17,700-square-foot mansion in 1991, and decades later listed the estate for $90 million
Article Text:
Representative image of an aerial view of Malibu coast (Image Credit: Unsplash)

The O.C.

Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me.

Mediterranean architecture and interior design

Representative image of cliffside coastline of Point Dume (Image Credit: Unsplash)

The dynamics of the real estate market

The luxury real estate market is seeing the entry of the largest cliffside residential property on Malibu’s Point Dume with a staggering price tag of $90 million according to the Wall Street Journal.The 1.16-acre property, beyond its architectural grandeur, comes with pop culture status, having served as a backdrop for Hollywood movies and series includingandHistorically known as Venezia Pacifica, the custom-built mansion was completed in 1991, following the couple's 1988 land purchase, and is being offered for sale for the first time by its original owners. Property records cited by the paper show the property was acquired in 1988 by the late real estate developer Ken Harges and his wife, Lorelei Harges, for $1.7 million. Since the passing of Ken Harges in 2016, and his wife later on, their daughters Bonnie Furgurson and Wendy Geweke have decided to list the multi-million-dollar asset due to immense logistical challenges required in managing an estate of this magnitude. The couple's daughters said their parents wanted to leave inland life for the California coastline.The primary residence incorporates a floor plan which is strongly evocative of classic Italian architecture, and inspiration from the couple’s historical travels through Italy has been etched directly into its structure. This sentiment for the region was echoed by their daughters, who wrote in a joint email cited by the Wall Street Journal: "Our mother was proudly 100% Italian," they said, "and together my parents drew inspiration from their many travels throughout Italy.The exterior is defined by classic columns, a signature terracotta-tiled roof, and an expansive circular motor court centered around a custom water fountain. Embracing 176 feet of direct bluff frontage, the estate’s perimeter overlooks the Pacific. Outside, the ocean facing grounds are landscaped with gardens and a sunken pavilion with columns to frame views of the immediate coastline.Inside, the architectural centerpiece is a massive, two-story central ballroom consisting of a sweeping glass curtain wall and an overhead barrel-vaulted glass ceiling. This expansive area is symmetrically flanked by a formal dining room on one side and a private library on the other. While the entry area showcases an artistic staircase alongside a custom glass elevator enclosed in decorative wrought ironwork. Throughout the estate’s nine bedrooms, the designs include coffered ceilings, structural columns, and intricate decorative millwork. Additionally, the primary bedroom suite is fitted with dual walk-in closets featuring motorized clothing carousels. Set apart from the living quarters is a 9,500-square-foot subterranean garage that can provide parking for 20 vehicles.The listing of the Malibu mansion is making its debut in a coastal submarket that is highly active. According to listing agent Chris Cortazzo of Compass, the broader volatility across the greater Los Angeles luxury housing sector has done little to dissuade the micro-market of Malibu, which continues to remain energetic.Ultimately, the extensive acreage's pricing draws precedent from a comparable oceanfront property located nearby at Little Dume Beach, which previously sold for $80 million.However, the caveat is that since Venezia Pacifica was constructed before California's coastal and building regulations and height limits grew stricter, replicating a compound of this specific scale and blufftop proximity would be difficult under current zoning parameters. This tension between regulation and property value is not unique to Malibu. A UCSB study found that properties within California’s regulated coastal zone were valued 18% to 25% higherthan comparable properties outside it. Researchers attribute the premium partly to regulations that protect ocean views and limit coastal development.
Article Summary: The 1.16-acre property was acquired in 1988 by the late real estate developer Ken Harges and his wife, Lorelei. The custom-built mansion was completed in 1991, following the couple's 1988 land purchase, and is being offered for sale for the first time by its original owners. The primary residence incorporates a floor plan which is strongly evocative of classic Italian architecture.

Article Title: In 2023, Steven Cohen paid $19.2 million for a Nantucket mansion; he then sought approval to demolish the six-bedroom main house
Article Text:
Representative image of an aerial view of coastline (Image Credits: Pexels)

The plan to swap size for a complete overhaul

Representative image of a luxury residential property in Nantucket. (Image Credits: Pexels)

The proposal was met with opposition from a neighbour

A newly constructed waterfront mansion on Nantucket could be headed for the wrecking ball soon after it changed hands. Sold for $19.2 million in November 2023, the home became the subject of a demolition proposal in 2024, according to the NY Post. Steven Cohen, identified as the buyer by NY Post, became the owner of the six-bedroom home through a blind trust in November 2023.According to Nantucket Current, Cohen filed a proposal with the Nantucket Historic District Commission (HDC), requesting permission to raze the multi-million-dollar residence.The request was scheduled for an official commission hearing and drew scrutiny from a local resident. Despite its high-end architectural design, the proposal outlines plans to demolish the estate in its entirety. The owner intends to replace the property's current footprint with a smaller one, consisting of a new 3,426-square-foot primary residence alongside a 528-square-foot detached guest house.Initially completed in 2022 following a collaborative effort that involved several designers and builders, the property consists of a main house decked with six bedrooms and a two-bedroom guest house, offering eight bedrooms in total.Previously listed on the market by J Pepper Frazier Real Estate, the property includes several luxury amenities It features a swimming pool, a pickleball court, direct beach access, and sweeping views across Nantucket Harbor.Although the home's high-end finishes and natural stone accents were elucidated in the promotional listing, the interior of the structure actually remained incomplete, as the owner's representative testimony revealed to the HDC in July. Representing the property owner, architect Matthew MacEachern of the island-based design firm Emeritus made clear the physical condition of the residence during initial structural reviews before the HDC.According to MacEachern, the mansion was merely a rough frame devoid of any interior finishes, despite having 90% of the windows fully fitted. MacEachern noted that while the new owner initially tried to work with the existing layout, the scale of the required modifications ultimately necessitated a comprehensive structural redesign, rendering total demolition and rebuilding necessary for the desired property layout.The proposal has triggered formal pushback from a next door property owner who remain adamant in resisting the repeated cycle of construction and teardowns within the neighborhood. Architect Graham Goldsmith, owner of an adjacent property on Pocomo Road, made his qualms clear to the HDC during preliminary hearings. Goldsmith asked, "How many more buildings are we going to tear down in this neighborhood? It just goes on and on. " Nantucket’s demolition-delay bylaw requires residential structures to be reviewed for reuse potential before a demolition permit can be issued.Goldsmith broached the demolition of a nearby 34-year-old mansion that belonged to Yankee Candle founder Michael J. Kittredge, questioning the sustainability of repeated neighborhood reconstructions. The regulatory power of the Historic District Commission remains strictly bound by municipal rules regardless of concerns about neighborhood consistency. HDC member Ray Pohl answered the neighborhood grievances by pointing out that the commission’s legal purview remains confined exclusively to reviewing external architecture and historical compatibility. Pohl maintained that any broader logistics, timelines, resource waste and teardown procedures remain outside the bounds of the HDC’s evaluation. As of October 8, 2024, neither Cohen nor representatives from the commission had issued any comments relevant to the upcoming scheduling or final decision on the pending demolition permit.
Article Summary: Six-bedroom mansion on Nantucket was sold for $19.2 million in November 2023. The new owner has filed a proposal with the Historic District Commission to demolish the property. The proposal has triggered formal pushback from a nearby property owner.

Article Title: Trump calls Sundar Pichai a 'monster' at White House event, Google CEO quips back
Article Text:
Trump calls Sundar Pichai a 'monster', Google CEO responds with a witty quip

US president Donald Trump appeared to jokingly describe Google CEO Sundar Pichai as a “monster” during an event, before clarifying that he was referring to Pichai’s stature and success.As Pichai began speaking, Trump said, “This guy is a monster, and nobody knows him. What a great life! To be a MONSTER and not have to go through this. All you have to know is — SUNDARR! Sundar is his name.”Pichai replied, “Hopefully a better tagline than I'm a monster!”This comes as US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said that he and a group of leading artificial intelligence company executives had signed a voluntary accord that includes internal and external reviews during a White House meeting aimed at addressing concerns over the technology.“I think I'm seeing tremendous self-policing. And they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump told reporters during an impromptu press conference outside the West Wing.Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson met with executives from major technology companies that are investing hundreds of billions of dollars in AI infrastructure, including data centres across the country. The projects have faced grassroots opposition from both Republicans and Democrats.The accord was signed by Trump, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Elon Musk, founder of xAI, which is now part of SpaceX.Posted by Trump on Truth Social late Tuesday, the accord leaves open the possibility of future regulation while outlining four voluntary steps for the companies. It calls for “robust internal controls”, cooperation with an “independent external auditor” to assess those controls, and the creation of a committee within each company’s board to review reports from internal and external auditors.“Over time, it may make sense to codify these steps into laws and regulations,” the accord said.Trump praised the executives for developing a technology he said would deliver “unbelievable growth”, while highlighting the economic impact of investment in data centres and related computer equipment.Amodei, who has been among the most outspoken voices calling for a slowdown in AI development, struck a more cautious note, saying, “The technology has very real risks.”"And, you know, the mechanism, how we address those risks is still under discussion,” Amodei said.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump appeared to jokingly describe Google CEO Sundar Pichai as a ‘monster’ during an event, before clarifying that he was referring to Pichae’s stature and success. This comes as US President Donald Trump said that he and a group of leading artificial intelligence company executives had signed a voluntary accord.

Article Title: Since 1987, a Massachusetts professor has taken the same photograph every day; after 30 years, the unseen record became a public portrait of aging
Article Text:
Representative image of a black and white triptych layout. (Image Credits: Leonardo.ai)

The process behind every portrait

Representative image of a black and white strip (Image Credits: Pexels)

Through adversity, education and reaching the gallery

A Boston College professor reached the 30th anniversary of his art project in 2017, containing self-portraits he took nearly every day for three decades. Karl Baden launched the project on February 23, 1987, the day after American artist Andy Warhol’s death.Baden's lifelong endeavor, titled "Every Day," is quite self-explanatory, as it records human mortality and the gradual day-to-day progression of the natural aging process.The project’s timeline predates the rise of Facebook; when Baden captured his very first portrait, digital cameras were not commercially available. Even the public internet did not exist outside of the United States Department of Defense, and the word "selfie" had not yet been coined. Due to this unique history, gallery owners and media figures have christened the professor the unwitting creator, touting him as "father of the selfie" or the "original selfie master. "The project’s objective was to capture the biological process of aging. In order to pinpoint it as vividly as possible, Baden turned environmental and operational variables into constants. All portraits taken are framed to make only the head and face visible; he poses expressionless and shirtless against the backdrop of a white wall. Using a single, un-automated 35mm film camera mounted on a tripod, Baden keeps the exact same lighting configuration and background exposure consistent through every portrait.Moreover, Baden purposefully avoids letting his mustache or beard grow, and keeps his hair simply styled to eliminate any personal styling variables that might distract viewers. Such strict consistency ensures the viewer's focus remains on the one thing he cannot control: the natural, biological progression of his aging face."I try to make every picture as close to the last one as possible. I use the same camera, the same film, the same lighting, the same backdrop, the same facial expression," he explained to Boston College . For Baden, the project is the study of tiny, daily changes; his methodology remains unhampered by travel, and the photographs are sustained through a portable photo kit that approximates technical consistency away from home.The daily photographic streak has survived through personal hardships and life challenges. After being diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2000, Baden began chemotherapy a year later. Unfettered, he maintained the daily self-portrait routine from his hospital bed, and the subsequent portraits show a drastic shift from vitality to illness. Baden became noticeably thinner, and he says his eyebrows, the only lasting marker of the cancer after treatment, never grew backBaden, who joined the faculty at Boston College in 1989, has integrated the lifelong project directly into his academic curriculum. He gives students a unique assignment by providing them his portrait taken on the day they were born, with the task of altering the image to reflect their birth. Through the project, there has been only one instance when Baden forgot to take a picture, which occurred on October 15, 1991, while commuting between lectures at Boston College and the Rhode Island School of Design.Baden’s "Every Day" project has been exhibited publicly at prominent contemporary art galleries across Boston and New York City. In 2017, Baden, who intended to pursue the project indefinitely, made it clear that his work wasn't related to the social media craze; instead, it honored the foundational purpose of photography, which is to capture a singular point in space across the passage of time.
Article Summary: Boston College professor Karl Baden has been taking self-portraits since February 23, 1987. Baden's lifelong endeavor, titled "Every Day," is quite self- explanatory, as it records human mortality and the gradual day-to-day progression of the natural aging process.

Article Title: In 2007, a Colorado photographer placed cameras on shrinking glaciers; 15 years later, his archive held 1.5 million images now used to measure ice loss
Article Text:
Representative image of a glacier. (Image Credits: Pexels).

The evolution of continuous time-lapse photography

The New Yorker

Representative image of a photographer capturing glacier. (Image Credit: Pexels)

The painstaking task of archiving and its challenges

An extensive collection of 1.5 million images in time-lapse chronicling 15 years of global glacier retreat has been officially preserved and archived at the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) . James Balog, an environmental photographer and mountaineer, founded the Extreme Ice Survey (EIS) in 2007. The project aimed to capture the physical impacts of climate change in real-time across the world's most remote frozen environments. The massive repository was transferred via a physical hard drive to the NSIDC server systems at the University of Colorado Boulder. Now the project is a public domain research resource for glaciologists and climate scientists worldwide.Balog’s massive visual census is an expansion of his earlier works, documenting deforestation and endangered wildlife during his global travels. After hearing from others about weather changes, he discerned that the real story was to be found in the ice. With his background in earth science and master’s degree in geomorphology from the Institute for Arctic and Alpine Research (INSTAAR), he felt equipped to track changes in the cryosphere. Balog drew inspiration from photojournalists Robert Capa and W. Eugene Smith, who exposed societal crises, and hoped to bring the same focus to the natural world.The blueprint for the project was conceived during a 2005 assignment forin Iceland, where Balog was taking pictures of crumbling glacial termini (the locations where glaciers meet land or open water). He realized that static single-frame photography wasn’t enough to capture the continuous structural ice loss, leading him to come up with an automated, long-term monitoring system. In partnership with leading glaciologists Tad Pfeffer and Jason Box, he began building time-lapse systems that were encased in custom boxes and powered by solar arrays and car batteries.The technical construction initially occupied Balog’s residential garage, where his family provided assistance. His wife, Suzanne, and daughters, Simone and Emily, were all supportive, with his six-year-old daughter Emily assisting with pieces of equipment like turnbuckles.While Balog’s initial plan was to place 25 time-lapse cameras near the glaciers, the project expanded into a network of 70 cameras stationed in Alaska, Iceland, Greenland, Nepal, Austria, Antarctica, Canada, South Georgia Island and Glacier National Park in Montana. Each camera was programmed to take pictures of glaciers continuously around the clock for months and even years. This helped in creating an extensive database of physical changes on nearly every observed glacier.When Balog initially approached NSIDC while the project was ongoing, talks fell through because he wanted to put a restriction on access for education and non-profit use. Following the conclusion of field operations in 2022, Balog circled back to the institution and agreed to an open science framework.However, transferring the data proved difficult from the start because Balog’s team lacked the bandwidth to push 1.5 million images to NSIDC’s servers and directories were too large; what they needed was funds. Donna Scott, programs and projects lead, secured endorsements from the science team, and director Mark Serreze and Jennifer Kay, a CIRES associate director, stepped up to contribute funding. The transfer then happened by hand in a parking lot, where Scott was handed a military ammunition box containing Balog’s hard drive of 1.5 million images from the EIS project.Once the drive arrived, a dedicated team spent 60 hours downloading, reconciling and organizing the images, including removing more than 200,000 duplicate files. Reflecting on the data transfer, Balog said he wanted to show future generations that some people were paying attention.
Article Summary: 1.5 million images in time-lapse chronicling 15 years of global glacier retreat have been officially preserved and archived at the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) James Balog, an environmental photographer and mountaineer, founded the Extreme Ice Survey (EIS) in 2007. The project aimed to capture the physical impacts of climate change in real-time across the world's most remote frozen environments.

Article Title: BLF’s newly-formed female unit 'KAAD' attacks military convoy in Balochistan; claims nine killed
Article Text:
Image credit: X

The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has released footage of an attack by its newly formed female unit on a Pakistani military convoy in Turbat, claiming that nine security personnel were killed in the operation.The video, released through the group’s media cell Aashoob, shows fighters of the Karima Armed Assault Division (KAAD) firing at a three-vehicle Quick Response Force (QRF) convoy on the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) highway on September 22.The footage includes a female commander briefing fighters before the operation, along with training clips. It also shows the fighters opening fire on the convoy from close range. The group claimed that several military vehicles were severely damaged and that several personnel were injured. These claims could not be independently verified.BLF spokesperson Major Gwahram Baloch said the group’s Qurban unit supported the operation and helped its fighters resist an attempt by Pakistani forces to encircle them, while covering their withdrawal. He said Qurban unit fighter Chakar Murad, alias Dileep Jan, was killed during the attack.The video also shows KAAD members conducting snap checks of vehicles in the Mangchar area of Kalat. The BLF claimed that its fighters carried out a blockade and vehicle checks there.In a separate incident, the Baloch Republican Army (BRA) claimed responsibility for an attack on a Mari Energies Limited site in the Beh Loti area of Dera Bugti, using rockets and heavy weapons.BRA spokesperson Sarbaz Baloch claimed that three company employees were killed and several others injured. He said a clash followed between Pakistani forces and members of a local armed group. The BRA claimed nine Pakistani military personnel and three members of the armed group were killed, while six of its own fighters also lost their lives, according to The Balochistan Post.The Baloch Republican Guards (BRG) separately claimed that its fighters seized Haji Shehr and destroyed a local police station using explosives. It also said BRA fighters entered Eri Shehr, took control of government facilities and withdrew after the operation.KAAD is named after Karima Baloch, a pro-independence activist and the first woman chairperson of the Baloch Students Organisation-Azad. She was found dead in Toronto in 2020.
Article Summary: Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) claims nine security personnel were killed in the operation. Video shows fighters of the Karima Armed Assault Division (KAAD) firing at a three-vehicle Quick Response Force (QRF) convoy on the China- Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) highway.

Article Title: 'Technical issue': Pakistan blocks airspace for Russian flight carrying uranium for Bangladesh nuclear plant
Article Text:
Russia’s uranium shipment for Bangladesh’s Rooppur nuclear plant delayed (Image credit: Reuters)

Poll Vote & Share your view Should international diplomatic norms allow for expedited clearance of flights carrying critical supplies like nuclear fuel? Definitely Not at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Pakistan has denied airspace clearance to a Russian cargo flight carrying nuclear fuel for Bangladesh's Rooppur nuclear power plant, delaying the scheduled arrival of uranium for the facility's Unit 2. Pakistan later described the matter as a "technical and procedural" issue involving flight routing and airspace permissions.The nuclear fuel was scheduled to arrive in Bangladesh on September 24 but did not reach the country after the aircraft was not allowed to use Pakistani airspace. Russia has now proposed the first week of October as a new arrival date, according to Bangladesh officials as cited by news agency ANI."We heard that a cargo plane carrying uranium for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Bangladesh was scheduled to arrive on September 24. However, the flight was not given permission to use Pakistani airspace, so the uranium did not arrive in Bangladesh as planned. As of now, the exact reason for Pakistan not granting the airspace clearance is still unknown", ANI quoted Bangladesh's minister for science and technology Faqir Mahbub Anam saying."A new date has been proposed, with Russia indicating the first week of October for the uranium to arrive in Bangladesh", he added.Sheikh Mohammed Tauhidul Islam, joint secretary in Bangladesh's science and technology ministry, said preparations had been completed at the airport before officials were informed that the airspace was unavailable."We had completed all the preparations at the airport and were waiting, but the liaison officer from Rosatom told us that the airspace was not clear. So we couldn’t send it. It may need to be rescheduled", he said.Pakistan's high commission in Dhaka, in a clarification, said the matter was related to technical and procedural arrangements."Pakistan maintains an unwavering commitment to international diplomatic norms and processes all requests for diplomatic flight and overflight clearances within a standardised, predictable timeframe, strictly in accordance with our established regulatory guidelines and civil aviation protocols," ANI quoted it as saying."With regard to the reports being quoted, the matter appears to relate to technical and procedural arrangements concerning flight routing and airspace permissions, which can occasionally require coordination among the relevant aviation and other authorities and may result in adjustments to flight schedules", it added.The high commission also said the incident should not be linked to Pakistan-Bangladesh ties."Pakistan attaches high importance to its relations with Bangladesh, and it would therefore be appropriate to view the matter in its proper technical context and not attach undue significance to reports or narratives that may seek to misplace it to undermine our bilateral relations," it said.The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, Bangladesh's first nuclear power facility, is being built with technical assistance from Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom. The project comprises two VVER-1200 reactor units with a combined capacity of 2,400 MW.
Article Summary: The nuclear fuel was scheduled to arrive in Bangladesh on September 24 but did not reach the country after the aircraft was not allowed to use Pakistani airspace. Pakistan later described the matter as a "technical and procedural" issue involving flight routing and airspace permissions. Russia has now proposed the first week of October as a new arrival date.

Article Title: 'Took mobile phones, cash': Karachi football team robbed at gunpoint on Balochistan highway
Article Text:
Image credit X @Baloch_Nojawan

NEW DELHI: A football team travelling from Karachi to Quetta to participate in the Chief Minister’s Gold Cup tournament was robbed at gunpoint on a highway in Pakistan’s Balochistan province, PTI reported on Monday.Around a dozen armed men intercepted the Karachi District West team’s bus between Mastung and Sariab, and took away the players’ mobile phones, cash and other valuables. The incident took place on Monday evening, leaving the players without money.Team manager Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto said the armed men ordered all passengers to get off the bus before robbing them."The armed men asked all the passengers to disembark from the bus and then took away all mobile phones, cash, and other valuables. They also butted some of the passengers."After reaching Quetta, the team informed Balochistan’s sports minister about the robbery. The minister intervened to provide the players with daily allowances, according to the report.Muhammad Azam, secretary of the Sindh Football Association, an affiliated unit of the Pakistan Football Federation, said the team had travelled despite official warnings against using road and rail routes to Quetta."We didn't send the Sindh team and we advised all other clubs in Karachi to avoid going to Quetta by bus or train because of the security situation. The Karachi west team still went ahead and what we feared happened," Muhammad Azam said.He added that the Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa football associations had also not sent teams for the tournament.The incident comes days after two local cricketers were abducted from Dera Bugti.The highway connecting Mastung district to Quetta has become a hotspot for armed groups targeting travellers, PTI reported.
Article Summary: A football team travelling from Karachi to Quetta was robbed at gunpoint. Around a dozen armed men intercepted the Karachi District West team’s bus. They took away the players’ mobile phones, cash and other valuables.

Article Title: Child, forced marriages of minority girls in Pakistan flagged at UN event
Article Text:
UN rights event highlights risks faced by girls in Pakistan’s child marriages (ANI photo)

The impact of child and forced marriages on girls in Pakistan, particularly those from minority communities, was discussed at a side event during the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva.Speakers at the event raised concerns about girls being married at a young age and the consequences for their education, health and basic rights. The event was reported by Global Human Rights Defence, a UN ECOSOC-accredited human rights organisation.Naveed Walter, president of Human Rights Focus Pakistan and a human rights defender, pointed to the scale of child rights violations in Pakistan and the vulnerability of children who enter marriage at an early age.“Most recently, UNICEF gave the data about Pakistan. Ninety million women and children and girls have been affected by child rights violations. And of them, 4.8 million were under 15 years of age,” Walter said.Walter said early marriage can leave girls without access to basic education and expose them to serious health risks, particularly during pregnancy.“You know, dear excellencies and dear audience, that during pregnancy, millions of children have died.And you know, under 30 per cent of the children who get married even have basic education,” he said.The discussion also focused on Sindh, where women's rights activist Shagufta Kandhro highlighted the situation of girls who are married before reaching adulthood.“According to the National Commission on the Rights of the Child, 84,000 children between the ages of 10 and 17 are married, widowed and separated. Many of them have already left school, and many face serious health risks,” Kandhro said.Kandhro said 21% of young women in Sindh had been married before turning 18. She also flagged concerns around teenage pregnancies and limited access to maternal healthcare.According to her, Pakistan sees an estimated 61,000 pregnancies among girls aged 15 to 19 each year. Only 44% of pregnant girls in this age group receive at least four antenatal visits, she said.Kandhro also cited anaemia among girls in Sindh, putting the figure at 61.9%. She described this as the highest rate among the provinces.The speakers urged stronger safeguards for women and children and called for greater international attention to child and forced marriage, which they linked to gender-based violence.
Article Summary: UN rights event highlights risks faced by girls in Pakistan’s child marriages. Women's rights activist Shagufta Kandhro highlighted the situation of girls who are married before reaching adulthood. She also flagged concerns around teenage pregnancies and limited access to maternal healthcare.

Article Title: Motorcycle-borne gunmen kill 3 cops in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Article Text:
TTP suspicion after 3 traffic cops killed in Pakistan gun attack (ANI file photo)

Three traffic police officers were killed and three others injured in a gun attack in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Monday, the Associated Press cited police.The attack took place in Wazirabad Bazaar in Tank district when suspected militants on motorcycles opened fire on a vehicle carrying the traffic police.The attackers fled the area after the shooting, local police official Jamshed Khan said.No group has claimed responsibility for the latest attack. Police are likely to suspect the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which has carried out several attacks in the region. The TTP is a separate group from Afghanistan’s Taliban but is allied with it.The attack on police officials came two days after 'fidayeen' bomb blast in Dera Ismail Khan city in the same province. The suicide bombing killed at least 13 people and wounded over 30 others.Gunmen also opened fire on an ambulance that arrived at the scene. The TTP claimed responsibility for that attack.Pakistan has repeatedly accused Afghanistan’s Taliban government of allowing TTP militants to operate from Afghan territory and carry out attacks in Pakistan.Kabul has denied the allegations and said it does not allow its territory to be used against other countries.
Article Summary: Three traffic police officers were killed and three others injured in a gun attack in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Monday. Police are likely to suspect the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which has carried out several attacks in the region. The TTP is a separate group from Afghanistan’s Taliban but is allied with it.

Article Title: 20-year-old Azerbaijani woman allegedly drugged, gang-raped in Pakistan's Lahore
Article Text:
Azerbaijani woman, 20, allegedly drugged and gang-raped in Lahore; 3 booked (AP file photo)

A 20-year-old woman from Azerbaijan was allegedly gang-raped by three men in Lahore after being taken to a flat in the Defence Housing Authority area, news agency PTI cited police on Sunday.The incident allegedly took place after the woman, who came to Pakistan from Baku for business, was taken to a cafe by two women late on September 25. Police said three men joined them at the cafe around 11 pm and later offered to drop them in their vehicle.Instead, the men allegedly took the Azerbaijani woman to a flat, where they gave her an intoxicating substance and sexually assaulted her, according to police.She was later left near Lahore's Ghazi Interchange. The suspects allegedly took her iPhone before abandoning her.Police officer Anjum Bashir said the woman had been staying in Lahore's Raiwind area since arriving in Pakistan more than two weeks ago.Police have registered a case against three men and identified the main accused. Raids are being conducted to arrest the suspects, while their names have also been placed on the stop list to prevent them from leaving the country.The vehicle allegedly used in the incident has been recovered from the house of a relative of the main accused, Bashir said.Investigators are also examining the role of the two women who allegedly took the victim to the cafe.The woman has undergone a medical examination and police have registered the case under relevant provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code.
Article Summary: Azerbaijani woman, 20, allegedly drugged and gang-raped in Lahore; 3 booked. Incident allegedly took place after the woman was taken to a cafe by two women. Police said three men joined them at the cafe and later offered to drop them in their vehicle.

Article Title: 'Don't go back like this': Pakistan minister's throat-cut gesture to Afghan journalist backfires - video
Article Text:
Pak minister’s throat-cut gesture to Afghan journalist

Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif has faced criticism on social media over a threat-like gesture he made towards an Afghan woman journalist who questioned him about Pakistan's ties with the Taliban and its response to the treatment of Afghan women.The incident took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York.The video clearly shows that journalist asked Asif what message Pakistan had for the Taliban over their policies toward Afghan women and why Islamabad had not challenged those policies when the Taliban were considered friends."What's your message to the Taliban now? To change their policy towards Afghan women? Why at the beginning, Pakistan didn't teach them that," the journalist asked, according to a video of the exchange shared on social media.Asif interrupted her without answering the question and pointed towards her attire."Don't go back like this over there. They will... otherwise they will..," he said, while making a hand gesture across his neck.The gesture drew strong condemnation online, with several social media users saying it appeared to imply that the journalist could be killed if she returned to Afghanistan. Users also criticised Asif and the men accompanying him for laughing after his remarks.A user on X wrote: "This is an utterly disgraceful way for a senior government minister to respond to a woman asking a serious question.""A woman asking about the suffering of Afghan women deserved an answer not intimidation, mockery, and laughter," he added.The journalist's question centred on the Taliban's policies towards Afghan women and Pakistan's position on them. Social media users said the response and the gesture were inappropriate and appeared to carry a threat of violence.The incident comes amid fresh tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, with Islamabad carrying out aerial and drone strikes inside Afghanistan early Thursday.The Taliban also confirmed to news agency Reuters that 28 "fighters" were killed after crossing from Pakistan into eastern Afghanistan. The ruling-authority in Kabul also added that most of them were former Afghan security personnel.Pakistan called the strikes as "precision attacks" on 10 locations. Federal information minister Atauallah Tarar said the operation was carried out in response to drones launched from Afghanistan a day earlier.According to Dawn, Tarar said in a post on X that the strikes targeted locations allegedly used for launching and storing drones. He described the operation as "deliberate, precise, calibrated and proportionate and strictly limited to identified military objectives directly linked to the attempted attacks against Pakistan".Afghanistan has warned Pakistan of "dire consequences" over the strikes, describing them as blatant aggression."In this criminal aggression, four of our fellow Afghan compatriots have been martyred. The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan strongly condemns these blind and cowardly attacks in the harshest terms, considering them a flagrant violation of all principles, a blatant aggression, and a crime," Afghan government spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid said.Cross-border hostilities between the two neighbours have continued in recent weeks, with Pakistan carrying out military action, including aerial strikes, inside Afghanistan.
Article Summary: Pak defence minister Khawaja Asif made a threat-like gesture to an Afghan journalist. The journalist asked him about Pakistan's ties with the Taliban and its response to the treatment of Afghan women. Social media users said the response and the gesture were inappropriate and appeared to carry a threat of violence.

Article Title: At least 13 dead in suicide bomb blast near police post in northwestern Pakistan
Article Text:
Also Read:

Pakistani Taliban claims responsibility

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most important action the government should take in response to the recent attack? Increase security at checkpoints Strengthen military operations Enhance community awareness programs Focus on diplomacy with militant groups 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With AP inputs)

At least 13 people were killed and around 35 others wounded on Saturday when a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a roadside police checkpoint in northwestern Pakistan, police and rescue officials said.The attack took place in Dera Ismail Khan, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Local police chief Safdar Baloch said most of the injured were security personnel and passersby, with some in critical condition.According to Baloch, gunmen later opened fire on an ambulance carrying victims to a nearby hospital, killing a rescue worker and injuring two others.Two women and a child were also among those killed in the suicide bombing, he added.The Pakistan i Taliban, or Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), claimed responsibility for the attack. The TTP is separate from, but allied with, the Afghan Taliban, which returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021 after the US withdrew its troops.Pakistan has witnessed a surge in militant attacks in recent years, many of them claimed by the TTP and the outlawed Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a separatist group primarily active in neighbouring Balochistan province.Islamabad has repeatedly accused the Afghan Taliban of allowing TTP members to operate from Afghan soil and have demanded that Kabul prevent cross-border attacks into Pakistan. Afghan authorities have denied allowing their territory to be used for attacks against other countries.Dera Ismail Khan is near South Waziristan, a former militant stronghold where the Pakistani military has carried out several operations in recent years.In December 2023, a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at the main gate of a police station in Dera Ismail Khan, killing at least 23 security personnel in one of the deadliest attacks in the area. It was claimed by Tehreek-e-Jihad Pakistan, a small militant group believed to be an offshoot of the TTP.
Article Summary: The attack took place in Dera Ismail Khan, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The Pakistan i Taliban, or Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), claimed responsibility. The TTP is separate from, but allied with, the Afghan Taliban.

Article Title: Pakistan govt puts Islamabad on lockdown as Imran Khan’s party pushes ahead with march
Article Text:
Islamabad locked down as PTI prepares for Imran Khan march

Leaders of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party have vowed to press ahead with nationwide demonstrations demanding his release, as authorities tightened security in Islamabad ahead of the planned march.More than 1,000 shipping containers, many reinforced with spikes, have been placed to block roads, while sandbags have been positioned on bridges and a key highway leading into the capital has been closed. Public gatherings have also been banned in Islamabad, with 22,000 police and other security personnel deployed across the city.The government has also deployed security personnel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and closed the main highway linking the provincial capital, Peshawar, with Islamabad. The sweeping security measures have fuelled anger and frustration in the capital, with several businesses struggling to receive supplies.The measures to prevent Khan’s PTI from proceeding with the march come amid mounting concerns over the treatment of the former prime minister, who has been in jail since August 2023 following convictions in multiple cases.On Friday, PTI leaders announced that they would postpone the start of the march to October 4, a week after the original September 27 date, saying they hoped the delay would put further pressure on the government.The planned protest also comes amid the detention of three of Imran Khan’s sisters. Aleema Khan was detained last week, followed by Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, who were ordered to remain in custody for 30 days under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance.
Article Summary: More than 1,000 shipping containers, many reinforced with spikes, have been placed to block roads. Sandbags have been positioned on bridges and a key highway leading into the capital has been closed. Public gatherings have also been banned in Islamabad, with 22,000 police and other security personnel deployed.

Article Title: Pakistan goes bananas over giant gorillas dancing to Bollywood songs
Article Text:
Clips of these larger-than-life performers have been spreading rapidly online (Photo: AFP)

Pakistanis are going bananas over a trend that has crossed the Indian border: Giant gorillas, dancing to Bollywood music.Clips of these larger-than-life performers have been spreading rapidly online, turning them into the surprise stars of weddings, birthdays and other festivities.In the videos, guests can be seen joining in alongside the costumed entertainers, many of them visibly delighted by the unusual addition to their celebrations. The performers swing their oversized arms to pounding DJ tracks while partygoers gather round and dance, creating a lively, comic spectacle that has quickly drawn attention across social media.Behind the trend in Lahore is Shayen Zahoor, who runs Gorilla.co.pk, a business offering giant dancing gorilla acts for events across the city.Speaking to AFP, Zahoor explained how quickly the idea took off. He said the costume was ordered in early April and arrived by the end of the same month, after which the team wasted no time putting it to use.Once the suit arrived, he and his team lost no time getting started."We uploaded a reel on Instagram, and within just two days it reached a million views," Zahoor recalled.The overwhelming response convinced them to treat the venture as a serious business, and bookings soon began pouring in, with the public reaction proving remarkably enthusiastic."On the very first day, we received approximately 1,200 to 1,300 messages," he said, describing how curious would-be customers flooded his inbox.Many wanted to know whether the costume had genuinely arrived, what it would cost to book, and other practical details before making up their minds.What began as a single Instagram reel has since snowballed into a full-fledged entertainment phenomenon, with giant gorillas now a familiar, if unlikely, fixture at Pakistani celebrations.
Article Summary: Giant dancing gorillas have become a popular feature at Pakistani celebrations. The performers swing their oversized arms to pounding DJ tracks while partygoers gather round. A single Instagram reel has since snowballed into a full-fledged entertainment phenomenon. The trend has even crossed the Indian border.

Article Title: Pakistan govt crackdown forces PTI retreat? Imran's party likely to postpone Sept 27 Islamabad march
Article Text:
Imran Khan has been in jail since 2023

Pakistan minister says PTI has 'run away'

(With PTI inputs)

The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has decided to postpone its planned march to Islamabad from September 27 to October 4, party insiders said on Friday.The PTI had planned the march to the capital to demand the release of its incarcerated founder and former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan . The decision to delay the protest apparently came in response to the tough measures taken by the federal government to prevent it.According to PTI sources, the decision was taken at a party meeting and will be formally announced by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister and PTI leader Sohail Afridi.Earlier in the day, Afridi had asserted at a press conference in Peshawar that the planned long march would go ahead despite road blockades and other measures. However, he expressed concern over reports of nails being driven into roads at the provincial boundaries, questioning whether a conspiracy to “cut” Khyber Pakhtunkhwa off from the rest of Pakistan had formally begun.“Our long march will definitely take place. This time, we will definitely come out. Put nails on the roads, place containers or fire bullets, we will come out. We will end this corrupt system of fake rulers,” he told reporters.“Pakistan will not break at any cost and we will save Pakistan,” he added.Cricketer-turned-politician Khan, 73, has been held at Rawalpindi’s high-security Adiala Jail since 2023, when he was arrested following his conviction in a corruption case.Pakistan information minister Ataullah Tarar reacted to the reports by saying the PTI had “run away” because it had made “no preparations” for the march to Islamabad.“There are no preparations for the PTI’s long march either, and that is why they have backed out of this protest. If they have the courage, let them come and hold the march,” Tarar said.The federal government had placed shipping containers along Islamabad’s main roads, allowing them to be closed at short notice ahead of the planned march.Hotels in the Faizabad area of Rawalpindi had been closed, while restaurants and shopkeepers were directed to shut their businesses. Guest houses and transport terminals in Faizabad had also been ordered to close from Friday night.Thousands of security personnel were deployed in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, the capital’s twin city and home to Pakistan Army headquarters, to control Khan’s supporters.Tensions over the planned protest continued despite PTI chairman Gohar Ali Khan urging the government to open negotiations and warning against confronting political workers with force.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has decided to postpone its planned march to Islamabad from September 27 to October 4. The PTI had planned the march to the capital to demand the release of its founder and former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan. Khan has been held at Rawalpindi’s high-security Adiala Jail since 2023, when he was arrested following his conviction in a corruption case.

Article Title: 'Could endanger his life': Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest
Article Text:
Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest

Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan 's son Kasim Khan has urged Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) supporters not to march towards Rawalpindi's Adiala jail during the party's planned September 27 protest, warning that such a move could be used by Pakistani authorities as a pretext for a "counter" assault on the prison and put his father's life at risk.The warning comes ahead of the PTI's planned protest and march, which is being held to demand Imran Khan's release.The former premier has been in prison since August 2023 following convictions in multiple cases.In a post on X, Kasim said he had been asked to appeal to supporters against gathering near Adiala jail."I’ve been instructed to call on the public not to attempt to march or protest nearby Adiala jail on 27. I’ve heard from sources that this may be used as an excuse for the establishment to launch a “counter” assault on the jail (Which my father is being held in), which could endanger his life. Please do not give them any reasons for “accidents” to happen to my father during the protest," Kasim's post read.His appeal comes as security measures have been stepped up across Punjab ahead of the PTI mobilisation.The Punjab government has imposed Section 144 across the province from September 23 to October 5, restricting public gatherings of five or more people on roads and in public places. Authorities have also sought the deployment of Pakistan Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali.The restrictions have been imposed citing security concerns. A provincial notification referred to a "serious and imminent threat" to public peace and safety from militant and terrorist organisations and hostile intelligence agencies.The planned protest comes amid the detention of three of Imran Khan's sisters. Aleema Khan was detained last week, followed by Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, who were detained for 30 days under the Punjab maintenance of public order ordinance.On Thursday, the Lahore high court refused to immediately suspend the detention orders against Uzma and Noreen. The court issued notices to the respondents and sought their replies before taking up the plea further.The detentions have added to tensions ahead of the September 27 mobilisation.According to Dawn, lawyers for Uzma and Noreen told the Lahore high court that the two women were "non-political" and had been detained without sufficient legal justification. The court decided to wait for the authorities' response before ruling on their request to suspend the detention orders.Kasim had earlier criticised the detention of his aunts and other relatives and called for international attention to the issue.“This is a disgrace. Now my Aunts Dr. Uzma and Noreen, along with my cousins Shershah and Shahrez, have now been abducted as well. They have broken into my aunties' and cousins' houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation. No reasons for arrest have been stated," he said in a post on X.Pakistani authorities have said the preventive detentions and restrictions are linked to public-order and security concerns. The Punjab government's notification specifically cited threats from militant organisations and other security risks while announcing the province-wide restrictions.The September 27 PTI protest is expected to add to the political and security pressure surrounding Imran Khan's continued incarceration, with authorities tightening restrictions and increasing security in areas linked to the planned mobilisation.
Article Summary: Kasim Khan urges supporters not to march towards Rawalpindi's Adiala jail during the party's planned September 27 protest. He warns that such a move could be used as a pretext for a "counter" assault on the prison and put his father's life at risk. Security measures have been stepped up across Punjab ahead of the protest.

Article Title: Watch: Pakistan PM runs away from questions on Hafeez Saeed at UN
Article Text:
Pak PM skips questions at UN

Hafiz Saeed named in terror cases

India hits out at Pakistan at UN

Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday declined to answer questions from reporters about Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder Hafiz Saeed during his visit to the United Nations headquarters for the 81st UN General Assembly.As Sharif entered the UN headquarters, reporters asked him, “Prime Minister, when will you stop harbouring terrorists?” Sharif did not respond. Later, as he left the premises, he was again asked when Pakistan would prosecute Saeed, but the prime minister once again declined to answer.Hafiz Muhammad Saeed, founder of the proscribed LeT, is a designated terrorist under India's Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and is wanted as an accused in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attack case.The National Investigation Agency has also named Saeed as an accused in its supplementary chargesheet in the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack case. The NIA has alleged that Pakistan-based LeT operatives were involved in the attack and has named Saeed as Accused No. 8 in the alleged larger conspiracy.A day earlier, India criticised Pakistan at the United Nations, accusing Islamabad of focusing on territorial claims and cross-border terrorism instead of addressing its economic and domestic challenges.Exercising India's right of reply at the UN Human Rights Council, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi said Pakistan should focus on development rather than “coveting territory of others or exporting terror”.Tyagi also accused Pakistan of suppressing civilians in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and referred to reports of deaths, arrests and restrictions on essential supplies including food, fuel and medicine.
Article Summary: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday declined to answer questions from reporters about Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder Hafiz Saeed. As Sharif entered the UN headquarters, reporters asked him, “Prime Minister, when will you stop harbouring terrorists?” Sharif did not respond.
