Article Title: Kabul-Islamabad tensions soar: Pakistan strikes 10 sites in Afghanistan after drone attacks
Article Text:
Taliban government spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid had denied on Wednesday that Afghan Taliban forces carried out attacks against Pakistan.

Pakistan accuses Taliban of backing militants

Escalation threatens mediation efforts

Pakistan said early Thursday that it had carried out airstrikes on 10 sites in Afghanistan that it said were used to launch drone attacks against Pakistan.Pakistan's information minister Attaullah Tarar said the strikes targeted sites linked to what Pakistan described as attempted attacks from Afghan territory. He said the strikes were “deliberate, precise, calibrated, and proportionate” and limited to military objectives.The announcement came after Pakistani officials said Afghan Taliban forces had launched eight rudimentary drones and shelled Pakistani border posts after Pakistani troops foiled what they described as an attempted cross-border infiltration by militants.There was no immediate response from Kabul to the latest Pakistani strikes. Taliban government spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid had denied on Wednesday that Afghan Taliban forces carried out attacks against Pakistan.According to four Pakistani officials, the attempted infiltration took place near Afghan border posts in Paktia and Nangarhar provinces. The militants were described by Islamabad as Fitna-ul-Khawarij, a term it uses for the Pakistani Taliban, or Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).The officials said Afghan Taliban forces allegedly provided support to the militants and later fired mortars and other heavy weapons at Pakistani border posts after the infiltration attempt was thwarted. Pakistani forces responded with artillery fire targeting Taliban border posts, mortar positions and defensive sites.The officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the latest escalation publicly, said some Afghan Taliban positions were subsequently abandoned and that there were casualties. The accounts could not be independently verified.Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Taliban government of allowing militants to operate from Afghan territory and carry out attacks inside Pakistan. Kabul has denied the allegations.Pakistani officials also said eight drones launched from Afghanistan were shot down before they could reach Kohat and the border town of Torkham. They said the drones caused no damage.The latest confrontation follows Pakistani airstrikes on eastern Afghanistan on Monday, which Islamabad said targeted militant hideouts. Pakistan said 28 militants were killed, while Afghan authorities reported at least three civilian deaths and four injuries. The UN mission in Afghanistan confirmed the civilian casualties, and Kabul formally protested the strikes.The latest fighting threatens mediation efforts by China, Turkey, Qatar and Saudi Arabia, which have been seeking to ease tensions between Islamabad and Kabul.The escalation also follows a series of deadly militant attacks in Pakistan's north-west. Six Pakistani security personnel were killed in a shootout with militants in Hangu, while a suicide bombing and subsequent gunbattle at a police compound in nearby Kohat killed at least 21 people.
Article Summary: Pakistani officials say Afghan Taliban forces launched eight rudimentary drones and shelled Pakistani border posts. Pakistani troops foiled what they described as an attempted cross-border infiltration by militants. Taliban government spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid had denied on Wednesday that Afghan Taliban. forces carried out attacks against Pakistan.

Article Title: Nepal rains: 27 killed in rain-induced disasters, authorities say
Article Text:
Beginning on September 24, Nepal faced catastrophic rainfall that triggered numerous landslides and floods, resulting in the tragic loss of 27 lives.

At least 27 people have been killed in Nepal by the rain related calamities since September 24, according to the authorities.The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) reports that eight people have been hurt in landslides and floods caused by severe rainfall, while four individuals are still unaccounted for.According to the administration, since September 24, twenty individuals have died in landslides, four in floods, and three in accidents involving severe rainfall.114 cattle were slaughtered and 1,082 households were impacted by the disasters. Additionally, 31 bridges were damaged by landslides and floods, and 227 homes were totally destroyed while 142 others were partially damaged.Between September 24 and 27, 542 rain-related catastrophe situations were documented, according to the NDRRMA.The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology reports say that over the four days ending September 27, 186 rainfall measurement stations nationwide recorded more than 100 mm of precipitation.At 544.2 mm, Dedhgaun in Nawalparasi (Bardaghat Susta East) had the most rainfall, followed by Panchase in Kaski with 500.2 mm and Atraulitaar in Tanahun with 472 mm.The meteorological experts attributed the severe rains to moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal and a low-pressure region near Uttar Pradesh in northern India.Over 980,000 individuals received flood-warning SMS notifications from the NDRRMA via telecom service providers.According to NDRRMA spokeswoman Shanti Mahat, some 2,000 individuals who were at risk of flooding were moved to safer locations. According to her, a helicopter was used to rescue people, who were stranded by landslides, and floods in isolated areas including Jajarkot, Myagdi, and Baglung.For search, rescue, and relief efforts, security troops from the Nepali Army, Armed Police Force, and Nepal Police were sent in.On September 27, a helicopter rescued 78 individuals, who were in danger in Pauddhar of Annapurna Rural Municipality-5 in Myagdi and transported them to a safe location, according to Mahat. Additionally, four individuals, who were stuck on an island in Jajarkot's Bheri River were flown, according to PTI report.According to local media sources, heavy rains caused landslides in Chame, Manang, on the afternoon of September 27. Flood and landslide debris from Ghatte Khola partially blocked the Marsyangdi River, allowing the two streams to join and form a lake.As the river surged, people in Chame and the surrounding regions evacuated to caves, forests, and other safer places. According to local media accounts, a bridge that had been buried started to resurface by Monday, and the lake's water level had dropped by around a meter.Along the Kaligandaki corridor, the water also caused damage to roads and bridges. Kantipur reported that the swelling river was cutting away portions of the road and causing landslides at many sites. Near Ridi and Rudrabeni, more than 50 meters of road were destroyed, and around 30 meters of road were cut at Dedhgaun.The NDRRMA sent out notifications to local bodies and authorities in the affected districts, requesting that they remove families residing in dangerous regions to safer sites and keep a high degree of surveillance in downstream areas.According to the NDRRMA, starting on September 28, water levels in significant rivers, including as the Narayani and Gandaki, began to progressively drop and the situation was generally returning to normal.The most recent floods and landslides occur, when Nepal is still recuperating from the catastrophic flash floods that occurred close to the border between Nepal and Tibet last month.On August 26, the Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border area, brought flooding downstream, destroying homes, cars, highways, bridges, and hydropower projects. Over 1,450 people were killed, and about 5,000 are still missing.
Article Summary: At least 27 people have been killed in Nepal by the rain related calamities since September 24, according to the authorities. Between September 24 and 27, 542 rain-related catastrophe situations were documented. Meteorologists attributed the severe rains to moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal and a low-pressure region near Uttar Pradesh in northern India.

Article Title: Malaysia sends 1,476 Myanmar nationals home despite UN warnings over safety
Article Text:
In a significant move, Malaysia has initiated a voluntary repatriation program for Myanmar nationals amidst safety concerns.

Malaysia began repatriating Myanmar nationals under a voluntary programme despite warnings from the United Nations refugee agency and rights groups that conditions in Myanmar remain unsafe.The first group of 1,476 people began their journey and are among 5,000 Myanmar nationals who Malaysia plans to repatriate in stages, news agency AP reported. According to Malaysia's home ministry, 10,388 Myanmar nationals were being held at immigration detention centres across the country as of August 15.A ministry official confirmed the repatriation. Buses believed to be carrying returnees arrived at a stadium in Manjung in central Perak state amid tight security. Ships believed to be from Myanmar were docked at the nearby Lumut naval base.The ministry said those in the first group had agreed to return voluntarily and would be transported using two Myanmar navy warships and a hospital ship. Details about their identities and individual circumstances were not immediately available.Myanmar has been facing armed conflict and political instability since the military seized power in 2021.The UN refugee agency and rights groups have urged caution over the repatriation programme, saying security and humanitarian conditions in parts of Myanmar remain volatile and that returnees could face serious risks.Malaysia hosts about 215,600 refugees and asylum seekers registered with the UNHCR, including around 126,000 Rohingya Muslims. The country is home to one of Southeast Asia's largest refugee communities.Malaysia is not a party to the UN Refugee Convention and treats refugees as undocumented migrants.The Rohingya have faced decades of discrimination and persecution in Myanmar, where authorities have largely denied them citizenship and refused to recognise them as an ethnic group. In Malaysia, they have also faced growing public hostility amid concerns over jobs, public services, security and the size of the refugee population, as well as misinformation and inflammatory rhetoric on social media.Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has defended the repatriation policy as a diplomatic effort to find a long-term solution. He has said Malaysia cannot host refugees indefinitely and that Myanmar must take responsibility for its citizens.Anwar said he plans to invite Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing to Malaysia to discuss the long-running issue of refugees and undocumented migrants.“I am inviting him to say that we can be friends and trade, we can accept Myanmar, but Myanmar must accept them back,” Anwar said in a podcast posted online on September 16. “To me, that's better diplomacy than just shouting angrily at Myanmar.”Myanmar foreign ministry official Han Win Aung said the plan follows repatriation operations in 2021 and 2022, when Myanmar received more than 1,100 of its nationals stranded in Malaysia.He said the repatriation involves genuine Myanmar citizens and is not intended to bring back Rohingya people.
Article Summary: Malaysia began repatriating Myanmar nationals under a voluntary programme. The first group of 1,476 people began their journey and are among 5,000 Myanmar nationals who Malaysia plans to repatriate in stages. UN refugee agency and rights groups have urged caution over the repatriation programme, saying security and humanitarian conditions in parts of Myanmar remain volatile.

Article Title: Watch: Government building collapses into river as heavy rains trigger fresh landslide in Nepal
Article Text:
Ward office building collapses in Nepal

A government ward office building in Nepal’s Baglung district collapsed into the Daram River due to a landslide triggered by days of heavy rainfall.A video showed a section of the hillside giving way and debris rushing downhill within seconds as the ward office building in Galkot Municipality collapsed into the river.The TOI could not independently verify the authenticity of the video.At least 10 people have died and one remains missing in Baglung after landslides struck several areas over the weekend, sweeping away homes and burying people, according to local authorities.Superintendent of police Phanindra Prasai, chief of the district police office in Baglung, said four deaths and one missing case were reported in Tamankhola Rural Municipality, while five people died in Nisikhola Rural Municipality on Sunday.Rescue teams, including security personnel supported by a Nepali army helicopter, have been deployed to affected areas.The landslides are part of a wider spell of severe weather across Nepal. According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), at least 21 people have died, five are missing and five others have been injured following four days of heavy rain, floods and landslides between September 24 and 27.Landslides accounted for 14 deaths and all five missing persons, while floods killed four people and heavy rainfall claimed three lives.Nepal is still recovering from the devastating August floods that inundated several villages, killing over 1,400 people and leaving nearly 6,000 missing.
Article Summary: A government ward office building in Nepal’s Baglung district collapsed into the Daram River due to a landslide. A video showed a section of the hillside giving way and debris rushing downhill within seconds. At least 10 people have died and one remains missing after landslides struck several areas over the weekend.
